data.name: Tale of Fallen Dragons
data.detailed_description:
Long time ago, there were nine sons born from Legendary Dragon.

These untamed dragons had bullied around and caused massive damage to the land since their birth. To end this chaos, the descendants of Five Elder Tribes joined together and released a powerful imprison spell. Finally, the dragons were defeated and kept under the Fallen Dragons Temple.

Those stories of nine dragons slowly faded from people's memory after several decades. Yet in the dungeon beneath the Fallen Dragons Temple, a new legend just begun...

Game Features
is a Roguelike game based on ancient Chinese story. In the game you will experience:
----More than 180 different items, which will have even more combinations.
----Randomly generated maps, every battle is a new challenge.
----Various sons of the Dragon, none of them is the same, and none of them is like the Dragon you have ever known.

Origins
After we finished our last game, we`re considering how to make something special on Chinese Culture.
In other games and comics, such as Kongfu and the Four famous novels are already very common to see. But there is still a lot to be discovered.

Finally, we choose “Artifact” as our theme, and make our story based on “Nine sons of the Dragons”.

So, here comes Tale of Fallen Dragons, a different Chinese style game.

Hope you`ll enjoy it.

Under the Fallen Dragons Temple, you`ll fight with various dragons which all have different shapes. The art style is based on real artifacts from China, we hope you could experience a different style of our culture.

reviews.review:
[b]Tale of Fallen Dragons[/b] is a rogue-like/lite dungeon crawler with a kind of randomly procedurally generated dungeon you must enter over and over.  You've been tasked by your master to find the rest of his students who have been trapped inside a kind of dragon dungeon.  He needs to seal the place up, but you must rescue all your peers before the process can begin.

You learn that you have special powers upon entering, and you are granted a sort of "weapon" that can change depending on what pickups you grab.  There is a vast array of different weaponry, and it is totally random what you'll find.  There's a vendor as well that you may randomly bump into.  Some weapons and upgrades have downsides, and some have tremendous upsides alone, so finding random items is key to making good progress.

The crafting system is nice too.  You have runes you can add to yourself as sort of equips.  You can add newly crafted runes to your rune setups to give yourself some passive bonuses to various attributes in the game.  

There are special rooms throughout with random occurences, enemy rooms that you must battle in before moving on, and boss rooms to clear the level and proceed to the next level.  Mini-quests are available periodically as you move from level to level as well, but they are a bit vague, and not as cut and dry as in some games.

Returning to the temple after death is where you may craft or add various new runes you earn upon death to your character, making them gradually stronger.


[h1]Pros[/h1]

A map feature, as well as instant teleportation between rooms, instead of having to walk through rooms that you've already cleared.

A box on the right side with a meter that goes up as you defeat enemies.  Gradually getting this meter to the top grants you that box on death, which then rewards you with runes to add or attempt to forge or combine with others for random results.  Every box you clear grants you the next level box.

A lot of weapons and items that change various aspects of gameplay.  Some increase stats at a cost, and others will just add passive bonus enhancements.  There is a lot to find!

The crafting system is pretty nice, since you might outgrow runes, so there is nothing else to do with them.  Care should be taken, since you never know what the result will be when forging or combining four together (called Compose). The Reforge system only takes two.  I'm still trying to figure out what the advantages are of one or the other...  Each level of rune can only be combined with the same corresponding level, which is indicated by colors.  The more boxes you earn before death, the better your overall loot collection will end up being.

I like the graphic presentation.  It has a nice Chinese flair to it, and it reminds me of a sort of graphic style of the dungeons in Recettear, or some of the Ys games, but much smaller squared rooms.  Definitely a Super Nintendo-esque vibe, with a bit more polish around the edges.


[h1]Cons[/h1]

I would like to see a controller vibration option.  I have my controller hooked up to the computer most of the time, and it will vibrate as I'm playing with the keyboard, so this feature would be "handy", no pun intended, for me personally.

The dungeon itself is a little bit monotonous.  There are rooms that are generated, but they start to get a bit boring, and the same kinds of enemies are on the levels, and there aren't a whole lot yet.  Keep in mind it is still early in the process.  I expect some improvements down the line some.

The language translations are a bit strange, and broken.  That being said, it's much better than a lot of other games I have played that were Chinese or Korean, or another similar language.  You can still pretty clearly understand what is being said or inferred for the most part.

The difficulty is a bit of a drag.  I have played other twin-stick shooters that seemed a bit easier to manage.  This one should probably have more difficulty options, or something similar.  I would eventually lose interest, since my progression is much slower with the rune collecting than the overall dungeon difficulty has been so far.

I would like more explanations for certain things in the game.  For instance, the crafting system.  I am just kind of blindly going into it, and it seems fairly random so far.  I don't know what compose is for, compared to reforge, for instance, and what the advantage of one would be over the other, aside from reforge needing only two runes, and compose needing four.  So far, using four hasn't shown any advantage over using two, so it seems pointless to use compose.


[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

This game is a lot of fun!  I would like to see more content added to keep me interested, and make me want to keep delving into the dungeon over and over.  I need a little more to draw me in, so to speak.  The artwork is very charming, and the music and theme is nice and feels very oriental to me.  The randomness is nice, but it makes me feel a little frustrated too at times, since I already feel it's a bit difficult beyond most twin stick styles that are similar to this game.  

If you're into this style of game, then I would recommend giving it a try, but if you are not a die-hard who would like to follow this and only this game in particular, I'd wait on more content before jumping in, or wait on a bit of a sale, unless you really like Early Access stuff.  The price for now is a little steep, but with more updates, this price may be more justified and reasonable.  Still, the game is really turning out to be very nice!  I am looking forward to seeing what is done in the future.  If care and time is taken, it could be very very good.  It's got a lot of potential and upside.
